question: Which of the following metals has the lowest melting point?
solution:
The correct answer is __Mercury__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Mercury__ is the only metal that is liquid at room temperature.
 
• It has an extremely low melting point of -38.83°C (or -37.89°F).
 
• Due to its low melting point, it is often used in thermometers and barometers.
 
• In comparison, other metals such as iron, lead, and gold have significantly higher melting points.
 
• Iron: Melting point is approximately 1538°C.
 
• Lead: Melting point is approximately 327.5°C.
 
• Gold: Melting point is approximately 1064°C.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Applications of Mercury:**

 
 
• Used in thermometers for temperature measurement due to its consistent thermal expansion.
 
• Used in barometers to measure atmospheric pressure.
 
 
 
• **Safety Concerns:**
 
 
• Mercury is highly toxic and can cause severe health issues if inhaled or ingested.
 
• Proper precautions must be taken while handling mercury-containing devices.
